- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+15% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment decay.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.5+ in 3 consecutive days), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in high-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment > 0.3 for 5+ days); apply 5–10% downward bias.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike (e.g., -10%+ from peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5 days if sentiment remains negative.
